title: Regional fallback routing & load-shed policy mismatch — after-action summary
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level summary: On 2026-02-12 we observed a multi-region degradation that resulted in sustained SLO misses for the hosted API for three hours. The immediate cause was a mismatch between region-prefixed routing rules and recently adjusted circuit-breaker thresholds combined with an aggressive load-shedding policy that targeted secondary regions. That sequence amplified traffic into a single warm region, which then experienced KV-cache cold-start tails and transient saturation. This ticket captures the timeline, root causes, interim mitigations, and an owner-assigned remediation plan to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~3 hours of elevated p95/p99 latency for text generation endpoints across NA and EU, ~12% overall request loss for non-critical tier, and several customer alerts. No data loss or security impact. Estimated availability impact: 0.8% SLO breach for the day for the hosted API.
timeline: 2026-02-12 09:05 UTC: First elevated latency alert (p95 increase) in US-East cluster observed by SLO monitoring.
2026-02-12 09:12 UTC: Automated circuit-breaker tripping in EU-West due to aggressive threshold tied to cost-tier. Traffic rerouted to US-East and ASIA-1 according to routing policy.
2026-02-12 09:15 UTC: ASIA-1 had insufficient warm-kv cache; many cold KV misses increased token-generation tails. Traffic concentrated onto US-East within 10 minutes.
2026-02-12 09:30 UTC: Load-shed rules executed in EU-West and ASIA-1; non-critical requests dropped aggressively. Customers received 429s and increased retries.
2026-02-12 10:00 UTC: Manual mitigate: routing pinned critical routes to US-East hot pool and temporarily relaxed circuit-breakers in EU-West for controlled failback.
2026-02-12 11:45 UTC: Metrics show gradual recovery; KV cache warm-up and autoscaler brought additional capacity online.
2026-02-12 12:10 UTC: Full traffic normalization confirmed; follow-up monitoring continued for 48 hours.
2026-02-12 12:30 UTC: Incident declared resolved; post-incident analysis initiated.
2026-02-15 14:00 UTC: Initial action list drafted and assigned (this ticket).
root_cause: Primary root cause: policy drift between routing layer and circuit-breaker configuration. A recent cost-optimization change tightened circuit thresholds for non-critical tiers in EU and ASIA without updating region routing weights and load-shed hysteresis. Secondary causes: KV cache warmup behavior not accounted for when rebalancing traffic, and autoscaler cooldown settings that delayed capacity during rapid reroutes.
mitigation_taken: Rolled back tightened circuit thresholds for non-critical tiers in EU and ASIA (09:50 UTC).
Pinned critical routes to dedicated hot pools in US-East to stop uncontrolled fan-in (10:00 UTC).
Relaxed load-shed aggressiveness threshold to allow controlled graceful degradation rather than wholesale dropping (10:05 UTC).
Triggered cache warm-up sequences for ASIA-1 and EU-West to reduce cold-KV tails (10:10 UTC).
Monitored and adjusted autoscaler cooldown to allow faster scale-up during reroutes (10:30 UTC).
follow_up_actions: (A) Reconcile routing weight config and circuit thresholds across regions — update config schema to require cross-region validation. Owner: Connor Reyes. Due: 2026-03-10.
(B) Add staged load-shed policy that uses token-aware priorities and allows slow warm-up windows before hard drops. Owner: Priya Natarajan. Due: 2026-03-24.
(C) Implement proactive KV-cache pre-warm on failover when traffic is rerouted; add synthetic warm-up requests during policy changes. Owner: Mateo Alvarez. Due: 2026-04-07.
(D) Shorten autoscaler cooldown on region failover events; instrument timeline to verify scale-up in under 4 minutes. Owner: Linh Tran. Due: 2026-03-17.
(E) Create automated cross-check alert that fires when routing weight changes are made without an accompanying circuit threshold update. Owner: SRE Tooling. Due: 2026-03-03.
(F) Run a chaos experiment simulating rapid reroute with KV-cache cold starts to validate policy changes. Owner: Resilience Guild (lead: Aisha Patel). Due: 2026-04-14.
(G) Update runbook: include step to pin routes and sequence a gradual failback rather than full immediate reroute. Owner: Runbook Maintainers. Due: 2026-03-05.
(H) Post-implementation SLO burn rate review for 30 days after changes; report back in weekly SLO review. Owner: Observability Team. Due: 2026-05-01.
notes: Key decision: prioritize predictable degradation over maximum cost savings for non-critical tiers. We agreed to defer additional cost optimizations until after resilient cross-region behavior is proven. The temporary rollback impacted costs for one billing period but prevented further SLO slippage.
review_feedback: PM (K. O'Hara): Ensure customer-facing incident note is prepared and synced with Support before circulation.
Design (N. Carter): Consider adding visual cues in Console for regions currently in relaxed circuit mode.
SRE (Jasmine Li): Add canary toggles for the new staged load-shed policy so we can roll back without config rollback.
Security (Elena Gomez): No secrets exposed; confirm that cache warm-up calls are rate-limited to prevent amplification attack surface.
